title: Psychosocial impact of maternal deaths and severe obstetric events on healthcare professionals
summary:
Background:
Severe obstetric events, including maternal deaths, can be highly distressing not only for patients and their families but also for the healthcare professionals involved in their care. In German-speaking countries, there is still limited systematic knowledge about how such events affect the mental well-being, professional functioning, and coping strategies of physicians and midwives.

Research question:
This study aims to investigate the psychosocial impact of maternal deaths and other severe obstetric complications on healthcare professionals. In addition, the study seeks to explore individual coping strategies, the perceived availability and use of institutional support services, and potential needs for future training and support interventions.

Methods:
In this multicenter observational study, healthcare professionals will first complete an anonymous online survey assessing trauma-related distress using a validated questionnaire. Subsequently, a subgroup of participants will take part in in-depth semi-structured interviews to further explore personal experiences and support needs. The findings are intended to contribute to the development of improved preventive and support measures for healthcare professionals working in obstetric care.
conditions: Trauma-related psychosocial burden in obstetric healthcare professionals following maternal deaths and severe obstetric events

interventions.name: Multicenter exploratory observational study using a mixed-methods approach. An initial quantitative online survey including validated questionnaires and demographic data collection will be followed by semi-structured qualitative interviews.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Employment as a healthcare professional in obstetric care (e.g., physicians, midwives, nursing staff).
Direct involvement in the management or care of at least one maternal death or severe obstetric event.
Sufficient proficiency in the German language to understand study information and participate in the survey and interview.
Written or electronic informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent.
Current acute psychological crisis or severe mental health condition that, from the participant’s or investigator’s perspective, precludes participation.
Insufficient language skills to complete the questionnaire or participate in the interview.
